Use case: style-transfer. Production animation cel sheet for Sam & Max Hit the Road HD.
Image 1 is the exact original pixel geometry to redraw on a 1536x1024 transparent canvas. Image 2 is the approved SAM model sheet. Image 3 is the approved MAX model sheet. Images 2 and 3 control identity and clean comic ink style; image 1 ALWAYS controls pose, crop, expression, local colors, positions, sizes and which parts exist.
Redraw the source cels at EXACTLY their present size and location in each quadrant. Both characters are in the SAME cel. Sam is a big brown dog with a long muzzle, black nose, small oval eyes, drooping ears, blue-gray fedora with black/white band, blue-gray suit, white shirt, blue/black striped tie, brown bare feet and cartoon hands. Max is a small cream rabbit-like creature with two long pink-lined ears, tiny black eyes, little pink nose, broad closed zigzag tooth grin, tiny torso and bare hands. In these source cels his legs are cropped to short flat stubs with a thin diagonal cream tail-like extension; do not add the complete feet from the master. Keep the source proportions; do not enlarge heads, eyes, hands or feet. Sam also has only short flat visible feet in these cels, not the large complete master feet. Preserve every partial crop from image 1 exactly.
Clean varied dark ink outlines with thin internal lines, flat colors and one restrained cel shade, matching the source blue-gray, warm brown and warm cream palette. Smooth the pixel staircases into natural curves, crisp coat folds and angular source teeth. No dithering, texture, gradients, halo, backdrop, floor, cast shadow, text, labels, panels, grid, watermark or extra props. Preserve every finger that is actually visible and the precise hand/cord contact. Keep all genuine small detached parts. Do not join separate parts across transparent gaps.
The orange/peach face-shaped object where shown is the game's ticking CARTOON EXPLOSIVE PROP with oval white eyes, a comic open mouth, an orange cord and little blue wire ends, not another body. Follow its exact small shape and its stretching/turning motion, do not invent extra anatomy or details. Paint it ONLY in cels that contain it.
Some frames deliberately omit heads, or include white window flash patches, or black character silhouettes. Preserve those source distinctions. Do not complete missing heads or cropped flying prop fragments. Bright magenta is padding and must become fully transparent with genuine alpha. Intentional opaque WHITE and BLACK shapes inside the sources must remain opaque.
Return precisely these separated cels, no others, all in the same positions on the same 1536x1024 canvas. Source-specific instructions:
UPPER LEFT: visible source 546x399 pixels at x=111,y=56. Sam raised arm reaches up; prop hangs close under fist, mouth and eyes as source. Max still.
UPPER RIGHT: visible source 553x392 pixels at x=875,y=60. Sam upright and smiling left, prop hangs beneath raised fist. Keep feet and stance. Max still.
LOWER LEFT: visible source 560x378 pixels at x=104,y=579. Sam mouth closed and stern left, same held prop and raised fist; Max still.
LOWER RIGHT: visible source 560x378 pixels at x=872,y=579. Sam mouth closed, muzzle slightly longer left, raised fist and hanging prop; Max still.

EXPRESSION LOCK: In every source cel 1934 through 1939 Sam has a small OPEN grinning mouth with a visible cream tooth strip near the far corner of his muzzle. Keep that visible tooth opening, never replace it with a closed smile. In 1940 and 1941 his mouth becomes closed as shown.

Image 4 is our own continuity sample of the SAME small prop. Use this SAME simple peach/orange face and BLUE wire ends in all four cels. NO hair or shaded scalp, red wires, goggles, extra teeth, eyebrows, tiny spots or invented wrinkles. Do not change the original cels: Sam smiles showing a small cream tooth opening in the top two frames and has a closed mouth in the bottom two. Follow these distinctions exactly.
